items.title: Measured Coupling for Parallel Decoding in Diffusion Language Models
items.summary_1line: Diffusion language models can write many tokens per step, but must choose which tokens are safe to commit together. Mean-field decoding penalizes pairs of positions whose predictions look alike. We replace this proxy with the coupling itself: how much committing one token changes
items.editor_note: Early context: diffusion LMs commit several tokens per step and need a better rule for which to commit together.

items.title: D-REAL: Acceptance-Length Optimization with Unbiased Gradients for Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoding efficiency depends on the number of consecutively accepted draft tokens, yet token-level training objectives do not directly optimize this quantity. We introduce D-REAL (Drafter Reinforcement of E...
items.editor_note: First drafter-objective paper: D-REAL optimizes acceptance length with unbiased gradients.

items.title: D3Tree: Learning to Prune Block-Diffusion Draft Trees for Efficient Verification
items.summary_1line: Block-diffusion drafters propose a whole block of tokens in one forward pass, and draft trees built from their position-wise marginals increase the expected accepted length of speculative decoding. Every tree node occupies a query row in target verification, so under concurrent s
items.editor_note: Prunes block-diffusion draft trees because every node costs a query row in target verification under concurrency.

items.title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoding speeds up language models by letting a lightweight drafter propose several future tokens that the target model verifies in parallel. Block diffusion drafters such as DFlash draft a whole block in one forward pass, and DDTree builds a draft tree from their per
items.editor_note: Builds fork-aware draft trees on DFlash-style block drafters, extending DDTree.

items.title: Phrase-Level Speculative Decoding on a Frozen Target
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoders raise throughput by banking more target tokens per forward pass, and Medusa, EAGLE-3, DFlash and DSpark all do it the same way: more candidates that survive verification. All of them draft in the target's own vocabulary, so one node of the candidate tree is o
items.editor_note: Drafts phrases instead of target-vocabulary tokens, against a frozen target.

items.title: REAL Loss: Optimizing Real Expected Acceptance Length for Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM inference by having a draft model propose multiple tokens for the target model to verify in one pass. The speedup is governed by the expected acceptance length (EAL), yet standard...
items.editor_note: A second loss aimed at real expected acceptance length, three days after D-REAL.

items.title: Callo: Serving Cache-Miss Requests with Speculative Decoding on Invalidated KV under Prefill-Decode Disaggregation
items.summary_1line: Agent sessions may involve frequent context edits, which effectively invalidate cached KV state and force requests to wait for re-prefill before decoding. We present Callo, a disaggregated serving system that leverage...
items.editor_note: Ties speculation to agent serving: decode on invalidated KV while re-prefill runs under prefill-decode disaggregation.

items.title: PACD: Provenance-Aware Consensus Decoding for Mitigating Cross-Modal Hallucinations in Omnimodal Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Omnimodal large language models (Omni-LLMs) integrate audio, video, and text for multimodal reasoning, yet remain vulnerable to cross-modal hallucinations, where one modality improperly influences predictions about an...
items.editor_note: Side branch: provenance-aware decoding against cross-modal hallucination in omnimodal models.

items.title: LoopCache: Accelerating Long-Context Self-Speculative Decoding for Looped Transformers
items.summary_1line: Looped Transformers achieve large effective depth with compact models by repeatedly applying a weight-shared block across R recurrent steps, each maintaining a loop-specific key-value (KV) cache. To accelerate sequent...
items.editor_note: Self-speculative decoding for looped transformers, targeting their per-loop KV caches at long context.

items.title: DistDNA: Language Model Fingerprinting under Stochastic Decoding
items.summary_1line: Behavioral fingerprints identify a large language model (LLM) from its responses to a shared set of prompts, enabling applications such as verifying whether a deployed model corresponds to the checkpoint it claims to be. Deployed models, however, are commonly served with stochast
items.editor_note: Side branch: fingerprinting which model is deployed when it is served with stochastic decoding.

items.title: Speculative Decoding Is Less Speculative Than You Think
items.summary_1line: Introduces DICE, a speculative decoding method that pre-samples verification randomness and uses it with an existing drafter to direct drafting toward likely continuations, reporting throughput gains of up to 24.6pp over baselines.
items.editor_note: DICE pre-samples verification randomness to steer the drafter; reports throughput gains up to 24.6pp.

items.title: Grammar-as-a-Draft: More Tokens per Speculative Decoding Step on Grammar-Constrained Structured Outputs
items.summary_1line: Introduces Grammar-as-a-Draft (GaaD), which merges grammar-forced tokens into speculative decoding draft rows for JSON, regex, and tool-call outputs, raising acceptance length and decoding speed in vLLM and Rust runtimes on TPU v7x.
items.editor_note: Grammar-forced tokens fill draft rows for JSON, regex and tool-call outputs in vLLM and Rust runtimes on TPU v7x.

items.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Contrastive Decoding for Hallucination Mitigation in Multimodal Large Language Models
items.summary_1line: Introduces CONCOR, a controlled benchmark that scores how contrastive decoding methods rank ground-truth objects against hallucinated candidates in multimodal LLMs, using a Contrastive Grounding Margin metric.
items.editor_note: Side branch: CONCOR re-scores contrastive decoding by how it ranks real objects against hallucinated ones.

items.title: Look Back, Draft Ahead: Corrective Prefix Attention for Parallel Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Introduces Corrective Prefix Attention, a parallel speculative decoding method that lets draft tokens attend to earlier choices in the block, reporting 13–15% more committed tokens per round than DSpark and up to 3.37× mean speedup on Qwen3 targets.
items.editor_note: Draft tokens attend to earlier block choices; 13-15% more committed tokens than DSpark, up to 3.37x on Qwen3.

items.title: Pando: Noise-Coupled Parallel Draft Trees for Efficient Edge Speculative Decoding
items.summary_1line: Pando is a speculative decoding method that builds dynamic draft trees on a parallel drafter using noise-coupled pruning, reporting 5.3x speedup and 4.2x energy reduction over autoregressive decoding for a 16-node tree on an edge device.
items.editor_note: Noise-coupled draft-tree pruning on an edge device: 5.3x speedup and 4.2x energy reduction with a 16-node tree.

items.title: LEGOSpec: A Composable and Efficient Framework for Speculative Draft Design and Training
items.summary_1line: LEGOSpec is a modular framework that splits speculative decoding draft models into four swappable components and trains them under matched conditions, yielding the DFlux draft that improves acceptance length on Qwen and Gemma models.
items.editor_note: Splits drafters into four swappable parts trained under matched conditions; its DFlux draft lifts acceptance on Qwen and Gemma.

items.title: Draft Calibration for Speculative Decoding: Accelerating LLM Serving by Matching Draft and Target Distributions
items.summary_1line: The paper applies post-hoc calibration, mainly standard temperature scaling, to the draft model in speculative decoding, reporting acceptance length gains of up to about 10% with almost no added cost across tasks.
items.editor_note: Latest item: post-hoc temperature scaling of the draft model raises acceptance length up to ~10% at near-zero cost.

editorial.tldr: This thread was regrouped around speculative decoding, so it is now a run of preprints on drafting tokens cheaply and verifying them in one target pass. Nov 7-10 papers trained drafters directly on acceptance length and built block-diffusion draft trees, then Nov 13-20 work moved into serving: invalidated KV caches, looped models and grammar-constrained outputs.
editorial.whats_new: Nov 24: three papers attack the drafter itself: temperature-scaling the draft model lifts acceptance length up to ~10% at almost no cost, LEGOSpec trains swappable draft parts under matched conditions, and Pando reports 5.3x on an edge device.
editorial.why_it_matters: Speculative decoding is a serving-side lever on decode latency and cost that leaves the target model's outputs unchanged, and this month's papers tune the parts an inference team actually owns: the drafter, the draft-tree shape, the KV cache and structured-output paths.
editorial.take_for_builders: If you run speculative decoding, log acceptance length per route before changing anything, then try the cheapest lever first: temperature-scale your existing drafter on your own traffic, and for JSON or tool-call endpoints check whether grammar-forced tokens can fill draft rows.

beats.headline: Train the drafter on acceptance length, not token accuracy
beats.summary: D-REAL and REAL Loss both argue token-level losses miss the quantity that sets the speedup: how many draft tokens survive in a row.

beats.headline: Block-diffusion drafters and smarter draft trees
beats.summary: Draft a whole block in one pass, then prune or fork the tree so verification rows are not wasted; a phrase-level drafter steps outside the target's vocabulary.

beats.headline: Speculation moves into the serving stack
beats.summary: Drafting over invalidated KV under prefill-decode disaggregation, self-speculation for looped transformers, pre-sampled verification randomness and grammar-forced tokens for JSON and tool calls.

beats.headline: Other decoding work grouped in by wording
beats.summary: Hallucination-mitigating decoding for multimodal models and model fingerprinting under sampled decoding; not speculative decoding.

beats.headline: Back to the drafter: attention, calibration, modular parts and edge trees
beats.summary: Nov 23-24 papers improve the draft side rather than the verifier, from cheap temperature scaling to a composable training framework.

open_questions: Do the reported speedups hold at production batch sizes and concurrency, where extra draft-tree rows compete for verification compute?
Does draft temperature scaling keep its ~10% acceptance gain when the target model or traffic mix changes after calibration?
Do Grammar-as-a-Draft or Callo land in a mainstream serving engine such as vLLM or SGLang beyond the authors' prototypes?
Does LEGOSpec's matched-condition comparison change which draft design (EAGLE-style, block diffusion, parallel) teams should default to?
Under the CONCOR benchmark, which published contrastive decoding methods still reduce multimodal hallucination?
